claim: In RyR1-ACP/Ca2+ inactivated, the high-affinity Ca2+-binding site remained fully occupied by Ca2+ up to 20σ.

claim: In RyR1-ACP/Ca2+ inactivated, there is additional out-of-plane tilting of the CD and CTD around the Ca2+-binding site.
source: Consistent with the second scenario, the high-affinity Ca2+-binding site in RyR1-ACP/Ca2+ inactivated remained fully occupied by Ca2+ up to 20σ, although with additional out-of-plane tilting of the CD and CTD around the Ca2+-binding site.
evidence: This is a direct statement of the structural observation.

claim: In RyR1-ACP/Ca2+ inactivated, the Ca2+ ion was coordinated by Glu3893, Glu3967 (CD), and Thr5001 (CTD) within contact distances of 2.8 Å.

claim: Mutations Q3970E/K in RyR1 are implicated in central core disease and equivalent RyR2 mutations in cardiac arrhythmia.

claim: The mutations Q3970E/K highlight the important Ca2+ sensing role for this residue.

claim: The RMSD (Cα backbone) between individual domains from RyR1-ACP/Ca2+ inactivated versus open was below 1.5 Å for all comparisons when the domains were pre-aligned pairwise, indicating little conformational change.

evidence: This is a direct statement of the RMSD analysis results and interpretation.

evidence: This is a direct statement of the RMSD analysis results and interpretation.

claim: In going from RyR1-ACP/Ca2+ open to RyR1-ACP/Ca2+ inactivated, there is an average shift of ~2 Å per domain, except for S6N' where the shift was ~0.7 Å.

source: Comparing the same domains between RyR1-ACP/Ca2+ inactivated and RyR1-ACP/EGTA (closed) yielded smaller repositioning with average shifts of ~1 Å, reflecting similarity in the domain's locations, with the exception of the EF hand domain that undergoes an ~5 Å repositioning (Figure 2B, Figure 2—figure supplement 2C).

claim: When the central blocks were pre-aligned as a unit using their respective CD domains, there was a good overlap between RyR1-ACP/Ca2+ open and RyR1-ACP/Ca2+ inactivated (RMSD below 1.5 Å) except for S6N′ (3.8 Å), revealing the bend in the middle of S6 upon opening.

evidence: This is a direct statement of the RMSD analysis results and interpretation.

source: This pulls the S6 helices (which are directly connected to the CTD) away from the pore axis, opening the ion pathway (Figure 2C and D).

source: To reach the inactivated state, the central block tilts further (see rotation axis in Figure 2—figure supplement 2B) in a movement similar to pushing down the levers of a winged corkscrew, which pushes each S6 helix 2.5 Å toward the pore axis, closing the channel.

claim: Alpha helices within the CTD act as a lever coupling the out-of-plane rotation to S6C′.

claim: ATP reinforces the connection between CTD-S6C′ in the presence of Ca2+.
source: Alpha helices within the CTD act as a lever coupling this out-of-plane rotation to S6C′ and as described further below, ATP reinforces the connection between CTD-S6C′ in the presence of Ca2+.
evidence: This is a mechanistic interpretation based on the structural observations described later in the manuscript.

claim: The EF hand domain did not show significant changes, with maximum Cα pre-aligned RMSD of 1.5 Å among the different states analyzed (closed, open, inactivated).

claim: The EF hand loops (residues 4081–4090, 4116–4123) were empty in the high Ca2+ conditions.
source: The EF hand loops (residues 4081–4090, 4116–4123) were empty in our high Ca2+ conditions, which is consistent with the low affinity of Ca2+ to this site (Kd 3.7 mM, Xiong et al., 1998).

claim: The low affinity of Ca2+ to the EF hand site is Kd 3.7 mM.

claim: The entire EF hand domain repositions noticeably during activation, with a 3.4° counterclockwise in-plane rotation (as seen from the cytoplasmic side), and 6.8° upward out-of-plane rotation.
source: Nonetheless, the entire EF hand domain, which protrudes from the CD-C′, repositions noticeably during activation, with a 3.4° counterclockwise in-plane rotation (as seen from the cytoplasmic side), and 6.8° upward out-of-plane rotation.

claim: The movement of the EF hand domain brings it in closer proximity to the S2–S3 loop.
source: This movement brings the EF hand domain in closer proximity to the S2–S3 loop (cytoplasmic loop between S2 and S3 TMD helices; residues 4664–4786) (Figure 3).

claim: With inactivation, an additional 1° counterclockwise rotation and 2.7° upward out-of-plane rotations define a physical limit to the counterclockwise motion, forming two salt bridges at the inter-subunit interface: Glu4075-Arg4736 and Lys4101-Asp4730.
source: With inactivation, an additional 1° counterclockwise rotation and 2.7° upward out-of-plane rotations define a physical limit to the counterclockwise motion, forming two salt bridges at this inter-subunit interface: Glu4075-Arg4736 and Lys4101-Asp4730, with their side chains within 3.5 Å (Figure 3A).

claim: The side chains of Glu4075-Arg4736 and Lys4101-Asp4730 are within 3.5 Å in the inactivated state.

claim: The interaction between the EF hand domain and S2-S3 loop is critical to support inactivation, as demonstrated by MH/CCD mutations facing this interface (F4732D, G4733E, and R4736W/Q) that greatly reduced channel inactivation.

source: On the other hand, MH/CCD mutations T4082M, S4113L, and N4120Y, in regions of the EF hand domain away from the interface (Figure 3B), did not affect RyR1 inactivation (Gomez et al., 2016), serving as a negative control for this hypothesis.

claim: The ATP-binding site showed full occupancy in the three conformations – open, closed, and inactivated.
source: The ATP-binding site showed full occupancy in the three conformations – open, closed, and inactivated.
